title: Heterogeneous instance throttling and kernel-profile reconciler for H100 / L40S / A10
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Objective: implement a reconciler that maps measured kernel profiles to per-instance run policies across heterogeneous GPUs (H100, L40S, A10) and dynamic GPU-slicing (MIG/instance-slicing) while adding a lightweight throttling layer to prevent cross-instance thermal/power cascades. This ticket covers design, experiments, and an initial implementation that: 1) collects microbenchmarks for prefill and decode kernels across clock/pstate settings and MIG partitions; 2) computes cost-latency optimal kernel choices per workload fingerprint; 3) exposes a runtime throttling policy that reduces GPU clocks or instance concurrency when sustained thermal or PCIe saturation is detected.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler service deploys on staging and attaches to the kernel-selection pipeline
Benchmarks showing >=6% median token-latency reduction for long-prefill (>=1024 tokens) workloads on H100 under mixed-concurrency compared to baseline
No regressions (>2%) in short-decode (<64 tokens) P99 latency across L40S and A10 profiles
Autoscaling/throttling guardrails prevent sustained device power limit violations for MIG partitions where applicable
Design doc and implementation PR merged with tests and CI microbenchmarks reproducible on the internal perf harness
implementation_notes: We will reuse the existing kernel-probe harness from ENG-9080 but extend it to collect: per-kernel memory bandwidth, achieved SM occupancy, and observed kv-cache eviction rates during prefill/decodes.

Kernel selector will produce a small decision table keyed by (model-arch, sequence-length-bucket, batch-size, device-profile) with fallback entries. Decision table serialized as compact flat file for fast lookup in the serving hot path.

Throttling will be opt-in by default and controlled by two knobs: concurrency cap per instance and a soft clock-reduction policy that uses NVML to pick a safe SM clock delta. This avoids hard resets and supports quick recovery.
MIG/instance-slicing: treat each slice as a logical device. For GPUs where MIG is unsupported, treat the whole GPU as one slice and annotate device-profile accordingly.
We will provide feature flags to ramp: experimental -> canary -> platform-wide. Initial canary limited to staging and 2 low-risk customers on dedicated capacity.
Make reconciler tolerant of noisy telemetry: use exponentially-weighted moving averages and require 30s sustained deviation before applying throttles.
Add tracing hooks to the console for visibility: decision provenance (why kernel X was chosen), throttling events, and before/after latency distributions.
planned_experiments: Experiment A: Sweep SM clock -200/0/+100 MHz on H100 for prefill of 2048 tokens, batch sizes 1/4, compare decode P95 and end-to-end throughput
Experiment B: Run same kernel-selection table on L40S with and without kv-cache recomputation to measure bandwidth pressure impact
Experiment C: Create synthetic mixed-concurrency load (chat + long-gen) on an A10 host with two MIG-like slices to validate isolation and throttling responsiveness
Experiment D: Stress PCIe reads by adding large embedding lookups while running decode to detect PCIe saturation thresholds and whether throttling reduces queue growth
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created. Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime and perf research. Assigned to Miguel.
2026-02-27: Pulled microbenchmark harness from ENG-9080 and added bandwidth counters. Initial H100 runs show kernel choice for prefill differs from A10 by 12% median latency.

2026-03-04: Discovered a regression when reducing SM clocks on L40S that increased decode tail latency for short sequences due to reduced tensor core throughput — reverted that parameter in the L40S profile.

2026-03-09: Implemented first reconciler prototype (PR #4873) that emits a decision table. Running canary on staging; telemetry shows 4.1% median improvement for long-prefill on H100 under isolated load.
2026-03-13: Added soft-throttle strategy to prevent power-limit oscillation. Observed reduced thermal trips during mixed-concurrency stress tests on H100 hosts. Preparing PR for review.
benchmark_results: H100 isolated prefill-2048: baseline median token-latency 22.8ms -> reconciler choice 21.9ms (4.0% improvement)
H100 mixed load (chat + long-gen): baseline median 33.5ms -> reconciler 31.5ms (5.97% improvement); P99 reduced by 8%
L40S short-decode-32: reconciler choice produced 1.2% worse P99 in one config; rolled back that kernel selection for L40S
A10 with two slices: throttling prevented PCIe queue growth; sustained throughput dropped 3% but end-to-end P99 improved by 12% under pathological synthetic load
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting decision table to synthetic benchmarks -> Mitigation: include production-derived traces and keep conservative fallback entries
Risk: Throttling applied too aggressively could violate SLAs -> Mitigation: throttle opt-in for dedicated customers, emergency rollback feature flag, and require 30s sustained metric before action
Risk: NVML clock changes might be disallowed in some cloud environments -> Mitigation: detect capability at boot and fallback to concurrency-based throttles
Risk: Additional CPU overhead from reconciler lookups on hot path -> Mitigation: decision table is a flat array stored in shared memory with O(1) lookup and microbenchmarked for <200ns overhead
decisions: Decision 1: Use small static decision tables for runtime lookup instead of an on-demand optimizer to minimize hot-path latency impact
Decision 2: Implement two throttling primitives: concurrency cap and clock delta. Prefer concurrency cap if NVML not permitted.
Decision 3: Treat MIG slices as logical devices; maintain per-slice telemetry and apply reconciler independently to each slice
Decision 4: Ramp via feature flags and canary customers before platform-wide rollout
